title: RE: Urgent Rotor Failure — Prairieline Lab Services

fields.to: Marcus Tran (Biosafety Officer); Dr. Anika Rao
fields.subject: RE: Urgent rotor failure, Lindgren 3rd floor
fields.body:
Good morning,

Thanks for the call. Our only certified rotor technician for Iowa is on a site in Omaha through Thursday. The earliest visit we can book is Friday, Oct. 16, 08:00–12:00. I've put a hold on that slot under service request PLS-SR-26-3318. Please confirm by end of day today so we don't lose it.

Until the inspection, please leave the rotor, buckets and lid in place, and do not run either centrifuge in that room.

Our records show the last rotor inspection on this unit was Aug. 14, 2025. We sent the renewal reminder in July 2026 to the contact address on the account, and it bounced. Please send us a current contact so it doesn't happen again.

We have a loaner unit available for $410/week, with delivery Thursday.

Attached from the lab manager: a phone photo of the failed unit's controller event log.
09:01:41 speed 21,000 rpm
09:01:52 IMBALANCE WARNING bucket 4
09:01:55 emergency stop, lid interlock held
09:02:10 stopped

Best,
Dana
fields.signature:
Dana Kowalczyk
Service Coordinator, Upper Midwest
Prairieline Lab Services
515-555-0163

instructorNote: This is a technical hurdle. The vendor can't come for three days, so the room stays closed. Watch whether the BSO decides on decontamination and verification for the second centrifuge or the room without promising Dr. Tomas Eklund a date. Also watch whether the PI logs the overdue inspection and the bounced reminder as corrective actions for the no-blame review under BSO plan section 8. Also hand over the controller event log from the failed unit (imbalance warning on bucket 4 seconds before the stop): it shows what failed first, not why, so players should not treat it as proof of cause.
